question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u={z}^{2}.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}=2z\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=z\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int z{e}^{{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =\int {e}^{{z}^{2}}\cdot z\,\text{d}z \\  & =\int {e}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {e}^{u}+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{z}^{2}}}{2}+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=2-3{t}^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=-6t\,⟹\,-\text{d}u=6t\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6t{e}^{2-3{t}^{2}}\,\text{d}t & =\int {e}^{2-3{t}^{2}}\cdot 6t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{u}\cdot \,(-\text{d}u) \\  & =-\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-{e}^{u}+C \\  & =-{e}^{2-3{t}^{2}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating Products Containing the Exponential Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=3-3{z}^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}=-6z\,⟹\,-\frac{4}{3}\text{d}u=8z\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 8z{e}^{3-3{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =\int {e}^{3-3{z}^{2}}\cdot 8z\,\text{d}z \\  & =\int {e}^{u}\cdot (-\frac{4}{3})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}{e}^{u}+C \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}{e}^{3-3{z}^{2}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
